scholarships.title: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS)
scholarships.official_source: Te Whare WÄnanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury, Scholarships Office

existing.description: The UC Doctoral Scholarship is a centrally funded Te Whare WÄnanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury award that supports study towards a first research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC. Its published value is financial assistance of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points. The same round can add recognition-only or top-up Prestige awards, but applicants who hold one of the Core scholarships are also automatically considered for Prestige awards with no separate application, and the Prestige value is added on top of the Core value (for example a $32,650 p.a. stipend becomes $37,650 p.a. with a $5,000 top-up). It is not a New Zealand Government scholarship; it is a university award and subject to funding availability and annual review.
eligibility: You intend to study at UC towards your first research doctoral degree.
Your GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study is equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0.
The award is available in any discipline at UC.
International students can apply for any UC scholarship unless the regulations specifically restrict the scholarship to NZ citizens or holders of NZ residence class visas.
Most scholarships require that you have admission to the University, so you must also meet the criteria for admission to your research doctoral programme.

You must have also submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications (point 2.2 of the Regulations); this is done in your myUC account.
You need to have created a myUC account prior to applying for a scholarship.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be entering their first research doctoral degree at UC in any discipline, with a GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0, and international students may apply unless a scholarship's regulations restrict it to NZ citizens or residence class visa holders.
benefits: Recognition-only award with no extra money: the Canterbury Scholarship, which recognises high-ranked domestic recipients of a centrally funded Core UC Doctoral Scholarship.

Prestige awards that add value on top of the Core award: Brownlie Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), William & Ina Cartwright Scholarship (Faculty of Education, $24,500 per 120 points of thesis enrolment), Doctoral Graduate Women Canterbury (Inc.) Trust Board Scholarship ($24,500 per 120 points, Arts, Education or Health), RÄtÄ Foundation Scholarship ($24,500 per 120 points).

The UC Commitments Doctoral Scholarship adds an additional $5,000 for research expenses across the duration of the degree, and UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships are co-funded with external agencies, but both are separate applications with their own project lists and their own closing dates (UC Commitments closes 27 October; UC Connect closes 15 September).

The UC Matariki Doctoral Scholarship and UC Pacific Doctoral Scholarship and the UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities are separate awards in the same round, the last running for up to 480 points rather than 360.
coverage: Financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points.
Tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points, as stated in the published value of the award.

Automatic consideration for Prestige top-up awards if awarded one of the Core scholarships, with no separate application; for example the Brownlie Scholarship and Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship each add $5,000 per 120 points to the Core value, and the Roper Scholarship in Science is $30,000 per 120 points of thesis enrolment.
requirements: Applications for the following doctoral scholarships are now open and will close 15 October: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS), UCDS for Students with Disabilities, UC Pacific Doctoral Scholarship and UC Matariki Doctoral Scholarship.
This application round is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before the 1 July 2027.

With the exception of the UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities and the UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships, students can apply for all other Core UC Doctoral Scholarships on the single 'UC Doctoral Scholarship' application form.
You must also have submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications.
These scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year.

Most UC scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports; some require an interview with the selection panel, and the Scholarships Office will notify you if one is required.
UC states that late applications are not accepted and that the closing date is not flexible.
documents: The UC application guidance lists the types of item you may be asked to provide: proof of citizenship or residency status (for example a birth certificate or passport).
Evidence of community involvement, financial hardship or ethnic background, where relevant.
List of referees; referees' reports are a written statement about your abilities from people you nominate.
Transcripts or records of learning, including Scholaro reports if your previous learning was at an overseas institution.
If necessary, an academic or language test.
Privacy provisions that you must sign and date as part of the application.
A CV only if it is specifically requested.
UC advises that if the scholarship entails a particular project, you should find out the full objectives and intended methodology of the project.
application_method: Search the UC scholarships database and read the scholarship's Regulations to confirm you meet every eligibility criterion.
Check the closing date for your round; UC states late applications are not accepted and scholarship applications are generally open approximately eight weeks before closing.
Create a myUC account if you do not already have one; UC states you need a myUC account before you can apply for any scholarship.
Submit your separate admission application for the research doctoral degree programme at UC in your myUC account, before the scholarship closing date (point 2.2 of the Regulations).
In your myUC account, click the 'Apply for a Scholarship' link and use the 'Search' function to find the scholarship.
Click 'Apply here' on the scholarship, which brings the application into your myUC account under 'My Applications'.
Complete the application. You can save and return to it. Attach every requested document and sign and date the privacy provisions.

Nominate your referees and make sure they know which scholarships you are applying for, the closing date, and what they must include; UC says it is your responsibility to ensure referees' reports arrive by the due date and the Scholarships Office will not follow up missing referee reports.

Submit the application before the closing date, then check that the status in 'My Applications' has changed to 'Submitted' and that you received an email confirming receipt. 'Request Pending' means the application was submitted but at least one reference is outstanding.
Await the outcome; UC states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and you will receive notification of the outcome in writing once the selection is final.
existing.selection_notes: UC states that most scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports, that some require an interview with the selection panel, and that selection committees vary according to the scholarship. It states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and the outcome is notified in writing once selection is final. The scholarship's own selection criteria sit in the Regulations document, which is not published on the pages read here. Prestige awards are awarded from the applicants who applied for a Core scholarship in a given academic year, with no separate application, and are awarded at the end of each academic year.
existing.best_fit: International and domestic applicants who intend to enter their first research doctoral degree at the University of Canterbury, can start before 1 July 2027, and hold academic results equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0 over the last two years of relevant academic study.
existing.notes: Not deferrable, not renewable, and no must-return-home or clinical restrictions are published on the pages read; treat all four as unconfirmed rather than as published terms. It is a university award, not an Australian or New Zealand Government scholarship, and UC states these scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year. The published value is $32,650 per 120 points plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment up to 360 points; UC does not publish on these pages a statement that living costs, travel, or compulsory course fees outside thesis-only enrolment are covered, so this must not be budgeted as full funding. If you intend to start your doctoral study on or after 1 July 2027 you are in the wrong round and must apply in the next round, which opens 20 March and closes 15 May.
existing.duration: Up to a total of 360 points of thesis-only doctoral enrolment (three years of full-time study)
existing.application_period: Two rounds a year. October round: opens 20 August 2026, closes 15 October 2026, for doctoral study starting before 1 July 2027. May round: opens 20 March, closes 15 May, for students starting in the second half of 2027. UC states applications generally open approximately eight weeks before the closing date.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for the October round close 15 October 2026. The round opened 20 August 2026 and is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before 1 July 2027.

eligibility: Must have gained admission into an approved doctoral programme at AUT before applying for the scholarship
Must have received an Offer of Place for the doctoral programme at AUT
Excellent academic record, normally first-class honours
Strong academic references and the potential for high-quality research
Open to all applicants including those from countries other than New Zealand who meet the admission requirements for a doctoral programme
existing.eligibility_summary: For applicants with an excellent academic record, normally first-class honours, strong academic references and the potential for high-quality research, who have already received an Offer of Place for the doctoral programme at AUT. The contestable rounds are open to all eligible applicants, including applicants from countries other than New Zealand who meet the admission requirements for a doctoral programme.
benefits: Tuition fees and compulsory student services fee
Automatic consideration for faculty or school funded options including a full fee scholarship or full fees plus a stipend of at least $20,000
coverage: Annual stipend of NZ$34,737 for 2026 awards
Tuition fees at the domestic rate
Up to three years of full-time study, or up to six years of part-time study
requirements: Admission into an approved doctoral programme at AUT before applying
Two academic referees must submit confidential reports directly to the scholarship portal by the closing date
Evidence of AUT faculty support if the proposed primary supervisor or head of school is not one of the referees
Complete the AUT Postgraduate Scholarship Contract in the portal for any stipend of $20,000 or greater
documents: Two-page statement outlining the proposed research, up to 1,000 words plus references
Brief CV of up to three A4 pages
Academic transcript(s) for any tertiary study completed at a university other than AUT
Copy of the conditional or unconditional Offer of Place
Confidential referee reports submitted directly to the portal
application_method: Apply for admission into the AUT doctoral programme and allow up to two months for processing
Register on the AUT online scholarships application portal and select the scholarship
Upload the research statement, CV, transcripts and Offer of Place
Request confidential reports from two academic referees via the portal
existing.selection_notes: AUT assesses applicants using criteria including GPA, research experience, and how the research aligns with AUT's research priorities. Incomplete applications are not forwarded to the selection panel. AUT awards scholarships to applicants with an excellent academic record, normally first-class honours.
existing.best_fit: Researchers worldwide with a first-class honours degree who have secured an AUT doctoral offer of place and can satisfy AUT faculty supervision and two academic referees.
existing.notes: The scholarship regulations state that the scholar must be resident in New Zealand and studying at AUT to take up the scholarship, and that stipends are not paid to students living off-shore. Short periods overseas for data collection and reasonable holiday leave of no more than one month in any one year are approved.
existing.duration: Up to three years of full-time study, or up to six years of part-time study at a half-rate stipend
existing.application_period: Three contestable rounds in 2026 closing 1 March, 15 July and 1 November. Applications open one month before each closing date, so the 1 November round opened on 1 October 2026 and is open on 2026-10-04.
